ARC-REV-01.rationale: The blocking rule for borrow, hold and renew is decided in Tier 2 (Accounts.isBlocked / ensureNotBlocked, called from Loans.borrow, Holds.place and Loans.renew). The change also removes an existing CLI copy of the rule (its own fines-minus-payments >= 5.00m check). Tier 3 views call Accounts.isBlocked and Accounts.owed and do not re-derive them. The CLI only branches on the Tier 3 view's Blocked flag to pick the output text.

evidence.quote: | Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added below Tier 4. The change removes the CLI's direct ports.Store.Load/Save and ports.Clock() calls and its direct call to Loans.renew. Renew and standing now go through Tier 3 use cases built on the existing commit/query helpers, which use the Store and Clock ports. The Tier 2 decisions stay pure.

evidence.quote: let isBlocked memberId (library: Library) = owed memberId library >= Policy.blockingBalance
blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The blocking balance has one definition, Policy.blockingBalance, and both the predicate and the refusal message reference it. What a member owes is always taken from Accounts.owed. The hard-coded 5.00m copy in the CLI is removed. 5.00 appears again only in test expectations.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-member-type blocking rule is decided entirely in Tier 2 (Policy.blockingBalance by type, Accounts.isBlocked / ensureNotBlocked). Tier 3 views only pass the member to Accounts.isBlocked. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code re-derives the threshold.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is introduced. The added lookups are pure operations on the library value inside Tier 2. No port is bypassed and nothing outside Tier 4 reads the clock or does I/O.

evidence.quote: (MemberBlocked(m.Id, activity, owed m.Id library, Policy.blockingBalance m.Type))
blocked until it is below {money blockingBalance}

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Each type's blocking balance is defined once in Policy.blockingBalance. The refusal message now uses the amount carried in the error instead of looking it up again, so the message and the predicate cannot drift apart. The decision document is updated to revision 2 to match. No literal is copied into Tier 3 or Tier 4.
